newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Hong Kong gold ends up on shortcovering.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong gold ends up on shortcovering.

text.p: Hong Kong gold ended up on Tuesday from New York's previous close, largely on European buying and shortcovering, bullion dealers said.
"Buying from Europe was the main reason," said one dealer.
Bullion ended at US$356.70/357.20 an ounce against New York's $356.00/50 close on Monday.
Other dealers said market players were shortcovering rapidly, believing that gold had seen its lowest point and was recovering.
But some said that attention was still focused on silver's rise, and that gold was just riding on silver's coattails.
The gold market remained short and there was still potential for shortcovering, dealers said.
Hong Kong traders projected gold would test $358 per ounce on the upside and then, if that level was breached, skip up to $360-362.
Local gold ended HK$34 higher at HK$3,295 a tael.
The carryover charge at the Chinese Gold and Silver Exchange Society rose to -4.00 from its previous fix at -6.00.
